exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Bargaining at the Market
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lin: How much is this beautiful silk scarf?
Seller: It's two hundred yuan. The silk is of very high quality.
Lin: That sounds a bit expensive for me. Could you lower the price?
Seller: Well, how much are you willing to pay for it?
Lin: I was thinking about one hundred and forty yuan.
Seller: That's too low. But because business is slow today, I can offer one hundred and seventy.
Lin: How about one hundred and sixty, and I'll take two of them?
Seller: All right, it's a deal. Two scarves for three hundred and twenty yuan.
exercises.translation_cn: 林问丝巾多少钱;卖家要价二百元,说丝绸质量很好;林觉得贵,请求降价;卖家问她愿出多少;林想出一百四;卖家说太低,但因今天生意清淡可降到一百七;林提出一百六并买两条;卖家同意,两条共三百二十元成交。

questions.stem: What does Lin want to buy?
What is the seller's first price for one scarf?
Why does the seller agree to lower the price?
options: Because the scarf is of poor quality.
Because Lin is a close friend.
Because the shop is closing forever.

questions.stem: How much does Lin first offer to pay?
What is the final deal they reach?
options: One scarf for two hundred yuan.
Two scarves for three hundred and twenty yuan.
One scarf for one hundred and forty yuan.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Chinese Travellers Abroad
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Each year, millions of Chinese travellers visit other countries.
When they spend money on hotels, food and shopping abroad, they help create jobs in those places.
In 2017, Chinese tourists made more than one hundred million trips overseas.
This spending is good for the countries they visit, and it is also a kind of trade.
As more people travel, the world becomes more closely connected.
exercises.translation_cn: 每年有数百万中国游客出国;他们在国外的住宿、餐饮和购物花费帮助当地创造就业;2017年中国游客出境超过一亿人次;这种花费有利于所到国家,也是一种贸易;随着更多人出行,世界联系更紧密。

questions.stem: Who travels abroad each year, according to the passage?
How does their spending help other countries?
How many overseas trips did Chinese tourists make in 2017?
What is tourist spending described as?
What happens as more people travel?
options: The world becomes more closely connected.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Returning a Faulty Phone
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Customer: Excuse me, I bought this phone here yesterday, but it won't turn on.
Manager: I'm very sorry to hear that. Let me have a look at it.
Customer: I've already tried charging it all night, and nothing happens.
Manager: You're right, it does seem broken. Would you like a free repair?
Customer: Considering all the trouble, I'd prefer a new phone or my money back.
Manager: I understand. I can give you a brand-new phone of the same model.
Customer: That sounds fair. Thank you for solving it so quickly.
Manager: It was our mistake, so there is no charge at all.
exercises.translation_cn: 顾客说昨天买的手机开不了机;经理道歉并查看;顾客说已充了一整夜电仍无反应;经理承认手机坏了,提出免费维修;顾客考虑到麻烦,更想换新机或退款;经理同意换一部同型号新机;顾客觉得公道并致谢;经理说是店里的过错,不收任何费用。

questions.stem: What problem does the customer have?
options: The phone is the wrong colour.

questions.stem: What had the customer already tried?
What does the manager first offer?
What does the customer ask for instead?
options: A new phone or a refund.

questions.stem: What does the manager finally agree to give?
options: A brand-new phone of the same model.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 The Hidden Cost
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Every choice you make has a hidden cost.
Suppose you spend a whole afternoon playing games.
The real cost is not zero; it is the homework you did not finish or the book you did not read.
Economists call this the opportunity cost.
Thinking about this hidden cost helps us make wiser choices every day.
exercises.translation_cn: 你做的每个选择都有隐藏成本;假设你花整个下午打游戏;真正的成本不是零,而是没写完的作业或没读的书;经济学家称之为机会成本;考虑这种隐藏成本能帮我们每天做出更明智的选择。

questions.stem: What does every choice have, according to the speaker?
If you play games all afternoon, what is the real cost?
options: The homework or reading you give up.

questions.stem: What do economists call this kind of cost?
What does thinking about the hidden cost help us do?
How long does the example afternoon of games last?

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A New Phone or Save?
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mei: My old phone still works fine, but I really want the new model.
Tom: How much more does the new one cost?
Mei: About a thousand yuan more than I had planned to spend.
Tom: Is the new phone really a thousand yuan better than your old one?
Mei: Hmm, when you put it that way, maybe not.
Tom: You could save that money for your summer trip instead.
Mei: You're right. The extra features just aren't worth the extra cost.
Tom: That's smart thinking. Your old phone is still good enough.
exercises.translation_cn: 梅说旧手机还能用,但很想要新款;汤姆问新机贵多少;梅说比预算多约一千元;汤姆问新机真比旧机好一千元吗;梅说这么一想也许不值;汤姆建议把钱留作暑假旅行;梅认同,额外功能不值额外成本;汤姆夸她想得明智,旧手机仍够用。

questions.stem: What does Mei want at the start?
How much more does the new phone cost?
options: Exactly the same as the old one.
About a thousand yuan more than planned.

questions.stem: What question does Tom ask Mei to think about?
options: Whether the new phone is worth the extra cost.

questions.stem: What does Tom suggest doing with the money?
options: Saving it for her summer trip.

questions.stem: What does Mei finally decide?
options: She must buy the new phone today.
Her old phone is useless now.
The extra features aren't worth the extra cost.
She will never use a phone again.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 How One Yuan Travels
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Money does not stay still; it travels through the whole economy.
Imagine you put one yuan into the bank.
The bank can lend that yuan to a builder, who pays it to a worker.
The worker then spends it at a shop, and the shopkeeper saves it in the bank again.
In this way, a single coin can help many different people earn a living.
exercises.translation_cn: 钱不会静止,它在整个经济中流动;假设你把一元存进银行;银行可把它借给建筑工,后者付给工人;工人在商店花掉,店主又存进银行;这样一枚硬币能帮助许多不同的人谋生。

options: It always stays in one place.
